summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Horizon Med through org and project keys, rate limiting and tenant-level quotas. Discussion covered hosted vs dedicated routing, per-project burst capacity, billing attribution, and security controls (KMS, RBAC, audit logs). Horizon requested pricing + POC steps; agreed to POC kickoff pending infra details.
transcript:
00:00 Alex (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, um were gonna walk through org and project keys and how rate limiting and quotas work on redwood, quick round of intros?
00:08 Dr. Priya Mehta (Horizon): hi this is priya, director of data science. thanks for doing this.
00:11 Tom Alvarez (Horizon IT): tom here, security/infra.
00:13 Maya Singh (Platform): maya, platform engineering.
00:15 Evan Brooks (Procurement): evan from procurement.
:00:18 Alex: awesome, and i'm alex, ae, and with me is samir our se, and leah in solutions, well keep it practical. if you have questions just jump in.
01:02 Samir (Redwood SE): cool, quick agenda: overview of org vs project keys, demo in the console, API examples, then policy rules for rate limits and burst, and finally POC/pricing.
01:18 Maya: sounds good. we're mainly worried about multi-tenant attribution and making sure one tenant can't blow out cost for others.
01:26 Alex: totally, that's the common ask. priya, quick context — are you planning hosted or private deployment for POC?
01:34 Dr. Priya: initially hosted but we may go private for PHI workloads later. we need SSO, kms integration, and audit logs.
01:41 Tom: and we need strict per-tenant quotas and ability to throttle per project not just org-level, also ability to route to dedicated if needed.
01:49 Samir: yeah so redwood supports hierarchy: org key at top for billing and admin, then project keys for apps/tenants. you can set per-project rate limits (tokens per minute), burst windows, and also enforce global org caps.
02:12 Alex: i'll share my screen — showing console — login as alex@redwood-demo.
02:21 [screen share noise]
02:30 Alex: here is the org settings page, you can see org-wide default quota and then project-level overrides. for example we set org quota 1M tokens/day but project A can be 200k, project B 50k.
02:46 Maya: can we have dynamic quotas based on tenant SLA? like premium tenants get higher burst?
02:53 Samir: yes, we have policy templates. you can target by project key or metadata tag; we support rate-tiering and scheduled quotas. (mumble) also note caching and batching affect token counts but not the rate limit enforcement which is on request count and token accounting.
03:20 Tom: how do you handle bursts? if one project suddenly spikes, do you auto-burst into dedicated?
03:26 Alex: good q. we have burst policies: you can configure allowed burst capacity per project that draws from org "burst pool". if you exceed org pool, requests can be throttled or routed to a lower-cost model variant. for dedicated customers we support fallback to spare capacity or autoscale.
03:45 Dr. Priya: routing to lower-cost model variants — is that automatic? we are concerned about quality regressions.
03:51 Samir: you control rollout policies. automatic fallback is optional; we tag model variants as compatible and you can set failover rules. also we provide preflight evals to see quality deltas.
04:10 Alex: jumping to API — here's a curl showing project key in header: Authorization: ProjectKey pk_live_abc123. that key enforces the per-project quotas.
04:26 Maya: if we rotate keys, do calls in-flight break?
04:30 Samir: no, we have key grace periods; rotation is seamless if you rotate via the api or console with short overlap window. older tokens remain valid for X minutes to finish in-flight.
04:45 Evan: pricing — does billing attach to org or project? we need per-tenant chargeback.
04:49 Alex: billing is tied to org account but we provide per-project usage exports and billing-attribution CSVs so you can map cost centers. also auto tags in the console.
05:05 Dr. Priya: security: we require customer-managed KMS and SSO (saml). do you support HSM KMS orbring-your-own-key?
05:13 Samir: yes, for Private deployments we support customer KMS (BYOK) and HSM integrations; for Hosted we support customer-managed keys via cloud KMS in most regions — you can require encryption-at-rest with those keys.
05:27 Tom: audit logs — are they immutable and do they include token-level traces?
05:31 Alex: audit logs include request metadata (project key, user id if present, model, latency) and are exportable to your SIEM. for Private we can push logs to your s3 or syslog.
05:45 [short silence]
06:00 Samir: demo time — creating a project key: click new project -> name it "patient-portal-prod" -> set quota 100k tokens/day and burst 1000 tokens/minute -> attach tags: tenant_id=tenant_123, sla=premium.
06:28 Alex: now we'll hit the API with that key and show enforcement. firing a small script that loops.
06:40 [typing sounds]
06:50 Samir: you can see requests are accepted until we exceed 1000 tokens/min then we get HTTP 429 with retry-after header. transcript note: sometimes 429 message is phrased differently in the console.
07:10 Maya: what about sub-projects or environments? can we have project keys scoped to env staging/prod?
07:16 Samir: yep, projects can be nested by naming policy and we recommend separate keys for envs so rotation and quotas are independent.
07:30 Dr. Priya: for the POC we'll likely want a limited tenant set, maybe 50 tenants, with a mix of premium and standard. how does Redwood handle tenant onboarding at scale?
07:40 Alex: we have APIs to programmatically create projects and keys, and templates to seed policies. many customers integrate this into their onboarding workflow.
07:55 Evan: contractually we need guarantee on rate limit enforcement and SLA. is that in Dedicated only?
08:03 Samir: SLA-backed latency and uptime are part of Dedicated. Hosted has best-effort SLAs per tier but for enterprise we can negotiate. rate-limits are always enforced — the SLA is about availability, not per-project quota specifics.
08:20 Maya: curious about rate-limit store — is it centralized? we don't want single point of failure.
08:26 Samir: good question. enforcement is distributed with local leases, we use a strongly consistent control plane for policy sync but the token bucket enforcement is local on serving nodes with periodic reconciliation, so it tolerates network partitions gracefully. (note: paraphrase, transcript may miss some words)
09:00 Dr. Priya: can we have different enforcement for text-generation vs embeddings? embeddings can be heavy but we treat them separately?
09:07 Alex: yes you can create per-route quotas, so embeddings endpoints can have different rate limit and token counting semantics.
09:18 Tom: about RBAC — can we limit who can create project keys? and ensure only ops can set quotas?
09:24 Samir: yes, RBAC supports role-level permissions: org-admin, billing, project-admin, read-only. you can attach SSO groups to roles.
09:35 Maya: what about API logs redaction — PII concern.
09:40 Alex: we support request-level redaction rules and you can opt to scrub request bodies before they hit logs; for Private we can run scrubbing in your network.
10:03 [brief cross-talk]
10:20 Samir: quick note on multi-tenant routing — we support policy-based routing by project tags; you can route premium tenants to dedicated pools, standard to shared hosted. fallbacks can go to cheaper models.
10:40 Dr. Priya: when you route a tenant to dedicated pool, does that change cost attribution?
10:44 Alex: yes cost is reported per project and we can apply different charge rates; in billing export it will show dedicated usage separately.
11:05 Evan: procurement asks about minimums for dedicated.
11:10 Alex: minimum committed capacity depends on GPU types; we can share a baseline example in the pricing doc.
11:20 Samir: toggling to console: showing policy engine — you can write rule: if (project.tag.sla=="premium") { quota=200k; burst=2k; route=dedicated-pool-a } else { quota=50k } and preview effect.
11:50 Maya: is there a dry-run mode to simulate policies?
11:53 Samir: yes, policy preview runs your recent traffic against the rule set to show expected hits and throttles.
12:10 Dr. Priya: what metrics are in the dashboard? token consumption, request latencies, throttle counts?
12:16 Alex: token consumption per project, latencies, 429 counts, cost per token, and time-of-day heatmaps. you can export per-tenant CSVs hourly.
12:38 [pause]
13:00 Samir: demo of API client: code snippet shows passing x-project-metadata header for more fine-grained tagging, this allows per-caller attribution inside the same project key.
13:22 Maya: does that open us up to spoofing? any auth for metadata?
13:26 Samir: metadata is advisory; for stronger guarantees we recommend unique project keys per caller or mTLS. we also have signed request headers in Private deployments.
13:45 Tom: curious about attack scenarios: if a rogue tenant floods requests with valid key, how quickly can we throttle?
13:51 Samir: immediate — enforcement is on the edge so within a second youll see throttling. you can also set anomaly detection alerts to auto-block keys and trigger workflows.
14:10 Dr. Priya: how do we onboard with minimum ops time?
14:14 Alex: typical POC is 2-4 weeks: we provision test org, share demo keys, run bench tests, then integrate with your onboarding APIs.
14:28 Evan: outstanding question: do you integrate with our billing system?
14:31 Alex: we provide CSVs and APIs; customers typically ingest exports into their billing system. for deeper integration we can offer webhooks.
14:45 Maya: any limits on number of projects? if we have thousands of tenants?
14:48 Samir: no hard limit; performance testing is recommended. weve run customers with several thousand projects, the control plane scales horizontally.
15:05 Dr. Priya: ok let's talk POC specifics — we'll provide tenant list and expected QPS per tenant.
15:12 Maya: i can provide that, plus describe envs.
15:18 Alex: great — well need: tenant list, per-tenant expected QPS, which tenants are premium, and a contact for your infra for network setup.
15:29 [sound of typing, a link posted in chat]
15:40 Alex: dropping link to POC checklist and quickstart in chat (shared link: https://redwood.example/po c-checklist) — note: transcript may break link text.
16:02 Evan: ok procurement wants a rough price estimate for the POC and a commercial sheet.
16:07 Alex: i'll include a POC commercial sheet in the email.
16:15 Dr. Priya: security questionnaire — tom will send to you.
16:18 Tom: yes i'll attach SOC2 and SSO details.
16:30 Samir: quick note — if you need per-tenant encryption with BYOK for hosted, there are some region limitations, we'll call these out in the doc.
16:45 Maya: do you have a sandbox with sample data we can test with?
16:49 Alex: yes, we can provision a sandbox org with seeded tenant data.
17:05 [brief pause]
17:20 Samir: showing how to rotate keys via API: POST /v1/keys/rotate returns new key and marks old key with grace period. example shown.
17:45 Maya: is rotation auditable?
17:48 Alex: yes rotation events appear in audit logs with actor.
18:05 Dr. Priya: what's the rollback story if a policy accidentally throttles critical traffic?
18:09 Samir: policy rollouts are versioned; you can rollback to previous set immediately and we have a canary mode to apply rules to X% of projects first.
18:30 Evan: any downstream integrations for SIEM?
18:33 Alex: yes logs to splunk/elk/s3/syslog, webhook alerts to pagerduty.
18:50 Maya: okay final question — for per-project pricing can rates be different per project?
18:55 Alex: yes, you can tag and apply multipliers in billing export; ultimately you charge internally how you want with our usage CSV.
19:10 Dr. Priya: good — next steps?
19:14 Alex: recap: we'll send pricing and POC steps, samir will share the recording and policy examples, horizon will provide tenant QPS and security questionnaire answers, schedule POC onboarding week of 5/25.
19:30 Tom: noted.
19:35 Evan: thanks all.
19:40 Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up by end of week.
45:50 [call ends]
